subject: ela
intro: Each item gives you a short part of a story, poem, or play. Decide where that part falls in the whole text or name the simple job it does. Read the part included in the prompt carefully before you answer.

items.prompt:
Read this opening paragraph of a story.

"Maya lived in a small house at the edge of the woods. Every morning she fed the chickens, walked to school, and came home before dark. Nothing exciting ever happened, and that was just how she liked it."

Where does this paragraph fall in the structure of the story, and what job does it do?
items.answer: It is the beginning of the story, and its job is to introduce the main character, Maya, and her ordinary, everyday world.

steps: Notice the signal words: this is the opening paragraph, so it sits at the beginning of the story.
Look at what the paragraph shows. It tells who the character is (Maya) and what her normal life is like (feeding chickens, walking to school).
Name the structural job. An opening like this introduces the main character and her ordinary world before anything changes.
So the part falls at the beginning and its job is to introduce Maya and her everyday life.

items.prompt:
Read this short part of a story.

"The waves crashed higher and higher. The boat tipped, and the rope slipped from Theo's hands. He had only seconds to grab the railing before he was thrown into the sea."

Does this moment fall in the rising tension (climax area) of the story or in the calm beginning? Explain how you know.
items.answer: It falls in the rising tension, near the climax, because the danger is at its highest point and Theo faces the problem head-on.

steps: Look at how much tension the part has. The waves crash, the boat tips, and Theo nearly falls into the sea.
A calm beginning would set up the character or place with little danger. This part is full of danger.
When the tension is at its highest and the character faces the problem directly, the part sits near the climax.
So this moment is in the rising tension near the climax, not the calm beginning.

items.prompt:
Read this final paragraph of a story.

"At last the storm passed. The villagers repaired the broken fences, planted new seeds, and laughed together in the warm sun. Life in the valley was peaceful once more."

Where does this paragraph fall in the structure of the story, and what job does it do?
items.answer: It falls at the end of the story, and its job is to resolve the action by showing the problem solved and life returning to normal.

steps: Notice the signal words: this is the final paragraph, so it sits at the end.
Look at what happens. The storm passes, the villagers fix things, and life is peaceful again.
Name the job. An ending that shows the problem solved and calm returning is the resolution.
So the part falls at the end and its job is to resolve the story.

items.prompt:
Read the opening stanza of a poem.

"The morning sun spilled gold across the hill,
A gentle breeze made all the tall grass sway.
The little farmhouse windows shone so still,
As birdsong woke the quiet start of day."

What does this opening stanza do for the poem? Choose the job it does and explain.
items.answer: It establishes the setting, showing a peaceful morning on a hill near a farmhouse, and creates a calm, quiet mood.

steps: Look at what the stanza describes: morning sun, a hill, tall grass, a farmhouse, and birdsong.
These are details of time and place, which means the stanza is building the setting.
Notice the feeling the words create, such as gentle, still, and quiet. This sets a calm mood.
So this opening stanza establishes the setting and the calm mood of the poem.

items.prompt:
Read this part of a play.

LENA: I cannot believe you told everyone my secret!
ROSA: I am sorry. I did not mean for it to spread.
LENA: Sorry is not enough. I trusted you, and now I cannot.

What job does this part do for the play as a whole?
items.answer: It introduces the conflict between Lena and Rosa, setting up the argument that will drive the rest of the play.

steps: Look at what is happening between the characters. Lena is angry that Rosa shared her secret.
A disagreement or problem between characters is a conflict.
Because this conflict is just appearing, its job is to introduce the problem that the rest of the play will deal with.
So this part introduces the conflict between Lena and Rosa.

items.prompt:
Read this short scene.

NARRATOR: It was the very first day at a brand new school.
SAM: (whispering) I don't know anyone here. My old friends are far away.
SAM: (taking a deep breath) Maybe I'll just find a seat in the back.

Where does this scene most likely fall in the story, the beginning or the resolution? Explain how you know.
items.answer: It falls at the beginning, because the words "first day" and "brand new school" show the situation is just being set up.

steps: Look for time signals. The narrator says it is the very first day at a brand new school.
A resolution comes at the end after problems are solved, but here nothing has happened yet.
A first day being introduced is a setup, which belongs at the beginning of the story.
So this scene falls at the beginning.

items.prompt:
Read this stanza from a poem.

"The night grew cold, the streetlamps dimmed to gray,
The empty sidewalk stretched on, long and bare.
The last warm window flickered, then went dark,
And silence settled heavy in the air."

Does this stanza mainly develop the setting or introduce a new character? Explain your choice.
items.answer: It mainly develops the setting, shifting to a cold, dark, lonely night with empty streets and a heavy, quiet mood.

steps: Look at the details. The stanza describes night, dim lamps, an empty sidewalk, and silence.
These are details about time, place, and mood, which build the setting.
No new character is named or shown acting, so it does not introduce a character.
So the stanza develops the setting and its lonely, cold mood.

items.prompt:
Read this opening paragraph.

"Diego had never been brave. He hid from spiders, jumped at thunder, and crossed the street to avoid the neighbor's small dog. But that was before the day everything changed."

What job does this opening paragraph do, and what does the last sentence hint about the story?
items.answer: It introduces the main character, Diego, and his fearful ordinary world, while the last sentence hints that a change or problem is coming.

steps: Look at what the paragraph shows about Diego: he is fearful and avoids things that scare him.
This is his ordinary world, so the paragraph's job is to introduce the character before things change.
Read the last sentence. The phrase "before the day everything changed" hints that a big change or problem is ahead.
So the part introduces Diego and his ordinary world and signals that change is coming.

items.prompt:
Read this part of a story.

"After weeks of practice, the day of the race finally came. Priya laced up her shoes, stepped to the starting line, and felt her heart pound as the whistle blew."

What job does this part do? Does it build toward the main event of the story or wrap it up?
items.answer: It builds toward the main event, leading up to the race that the whole story has been preparing for.

steps: Look at what the part describes. After weeks of practice, the race day arrives and Priya starts to run.
Words like "finally came" and "heart pound" show rising tension before a big moment.
A part that leads up to the main event builds toward it; it does not wrap up the story.
So this part builds toward the main event, the race.

items.prompt:
Read this short scene from a play.

MR. HALE: (entering the dark room) Who is there? Show yourself!
VOICE: (from the shadows) You should not have come here, Mr. Hale.
MR. HALE: (stepping back) Then I will find out why.

What job does this opening scene do for the play?
items.answer: It introduces a mystery and conflict, creating suspense by showing a strange voice warning Mr. Hale, which sets up the rest of the play.

steps: Look at what is happening. Mr. Hale enters a dark room and a hidden voice warns him to leave.
A strange voice and a warning create suspense and a problem to solve.
Because this is the opening scene, its job is to set up the mystery and conflict for the rest of the play.
So this scene introduces the conflict and builds suspense.

items.prompt:
Read this stanza, then answer.

"And so the lesson stayed with me through years:
That kindness given freely comes back round.
The smallest gift can dry a stranger's tears,
And quiet help is where true wealth is found."

This is the final stanza of the poem. What job does it do for the poem as a whole?
items.answer: It states the poem's message or theme, telling the lesson the speaker learned: that kindness given freely returns and is true wealth.

steps: Notice this is the final stanza, so it likely wraps up the poem's meaning.
Read what it says. It names a lesson about kindness coming back and being true wealth.
When an ending states the lesson or central idea, its job is to develop the theme.
So this final stanza delivers the poem's theme.

items.prompt:
Read this paragraph.

"The old library smelled of dust and rain. Tall shelves rose into shadow, and a single lamp glowed in the corner. Outside, thunder rumbled, and the heavy door creaked shut behind Ana."

Does this paragraph mainly develop the setting or resolve the plot? Explain how you know.
items.answer: It mainly develops the setting, describing the dusty, shadowy library and the stormy weather to create a mysterious mood.

steps: Look at the details: a dusty library, tall shadowy shelves, a dim lamp, and thunder outside.
These describe place, weather, and mood, which all build the setting.
A resolution would solve a problem at the end, but no problem is being solved here.
So the paragraph develops the setting and its mysterious mood.

items.prompt:
Read this part of a story.

"Just as the team was about to give up, Leo noticed a small door hidden behind the bookcase. 'Wait,' he said. 'I think I found the way out.' Everyone rushed toward him."

What job does this part do? Name the change it brings to the story.
items.answer: It marks a turning point, because Leo's discovery of the hidden door changes the situation from giving up to finding a way out.

steps: Look at the situation before and after. The team was about to give up, then Leo finds a hidden door.
A moment that changes the direction of the story is a turning point.
Here the discovery turns hopelessness into hope, so the part marks a turning point.
So this part's job is to be a turning point that shifts the story.

items.prompt:
Read this opening scene of a play.

NARRATOR: A quiet farm at sunrise. Chickens cluck, and a rooster crows.
FARMER GREEN: (yawning) Another peaceful morning. Time to start the chores.

What job does this opening scene do for the play?
items.answer: It introduces the setting and the main character, showing the peaceful farm at sunrise and Farmer Green beginning an ordinary day.

steps: Look at what the narrator and Farmer Green show: a quiet farm at sunrise and a normal morning of chores.
Details of place and a calm, ordinary day build the setting.
Farmer Green is also presented, so the scene introduces the main character too.
So this opening scene introduces the setting and the character before any problem begins.

items.prompt:
Read this short part of a story.

"For three days the knight had searched the dark forest. His food was gone, his torch was dim, and still the dragon's cave was nowhere in sight. He wondered if he should turn back."

Where does this part fall in the structure of the story, the calm ending or the middle where the problem is still building? Explain.
items.answer: It falls in the middle, where the problem is still building, because the knight is struggling and has not yet reached his goal.

steps: Look at what is happening. The knight is searching, running low on supplies, and has not found the cave.
A calm ending would show the problem solved, but here the problem is still unsolved.
When the character struggles and the goal is not yet reached, the part sits in the middle as tension builds.
So this part falls in the middle where the problem is still building.
